URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/ukraine-russia-war-live-putin-zelensky-oil-refineries-casualties-map-b3091150.html
The Independent, 25 November

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

BBC’s analysis of the records show 65 per cent of 18 to 24 year-olds who lost their lives in 2025 died in the war

BookmarkCommentsGo to commentsBookmark popoverRemoved from bookmarks

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

At least 490,334 Russian soldiers died since the start of the war in Ukraine in February 2022, according to leaked data from Russia’s federal statistics agency Rosstat.

The BBC Russian accessed more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026 after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow.

An analysis of the records show 65 per cent of 18 to 24 year-olds who lost their lives in 2025 died in the Ukraine war.

On the battlefield, Russian president Vladimir Putin warned that retaliation is “inevitable” after Ukraine continued to hit Russian oil plants despite Donald Trump’s requests not to do so.

Ukrainian drones struck two more major facilities overnight into Wednesday, with local residents reporting large fires at refineries in the Samara region some 800km inside Russia.

Putin told a meeting of government officials and oil executives at the Kremlin on Tuesday that Ukraine “continues to attack our refining facilities, despite the US president's appeal and direct request to refrain from such attacks”.

Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said Putin could end the attacks on refineries by calling an end to the ongoing conflict.

Photos provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Services show rescue workers puts out a fire of a building damaged in a Russian strike on Chernihiv region, Ukraine.

A Russian drone attack on the Ukrainian capital late on Tuesday sparked a fire at a 16-storey residential building and injured two people.

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said falling drone debris had set the lower two floors of the apartment block ablaze in a central district of the capital.

Both injured residents were treated at the scene.

Russia attacked Naftogaz Group gas production infrastructure in the Poltava region overnight, causing a large fire and halting operations at the site, Naftogaz CEO Sergii Fedorenko said on Wednesday.

In ‌a post on ‌Facebook, Fedorenko said ⁠it was not the first such attack and accused Russia of deliberately ‌targeting gas production ​to ‌deprive Ukrainians ⁠of heat ⁠in winter.

Russia’s defence ministry said on Wednesday that its forces had struck a cargo vessel in the Ukrainian Black Sea port of Chornomorsk.

It marks latest attack after several people were injured on 14 November attack in an attack that damaged energy infrastructure, an administrative building and residential properties.

The Trump administration has quietly abandoned proposals to use business deals as an incentive for Russia to end its war in Ukraine after the Kremlin showed little interest in proposed energy and aviation ventures, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner told European officials that commercial partnerships were no longer a central part of Washington’s efforts to persuade Moscow to end the war.

The report cited five officials briefed on the shift in the US negotiating strategy.

More than 1,000 Russian soldiers have taken their own lives since the invasion of Ukraine, according to a new report.

At least 1,087 military personnel ended their own life in Ukraine or in Russian border regions between 2022 and 2026, according to confidential data held by state statistics agency Rosstat and seen by The Guardian.

Leaked data from a corpus of 11 million death certificates shows that the trend has steadily increased since the full-scale invasion, with war and military-related deaths rising from more than 50 in 2022 to 365 last year.

A Russian attack has killed a man near Bila Tserkva in Ukraine’s Kyiv region, Tymur Tkachenko said on Telegram.

A commercial facility was also damaged in the attack, he said.

Bila Tserkva, a city of around 200,000 people, lies some 64km (40 miles) from the outskirts of the Ukrainian capital.

A drone attack has killed one person, triggered power cuts and caused damage on the ground in Russia’s Samara region, Russian news agencies reported on Wednesday, citing regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev.

The Samara region is a major oil refining hub for Russian state oil company Rosneft.

It was not immediately clear whether any oil facilities had been damaged in the attack.

Fires have been reported at two major Russian oil refineries in the Samara region, some 800km from the border with Ukraine, following apparent Ukrainian drone strikes.

The monitoring channel Exilenova Plus named the refineries involved as the Syzran and Kuibyshev facilities, according to the Kyiv Independent, with local residents sharing footage of a large fire at the latter.

Earlier, Vladimir Putin threatened to retaliate against Ukraine's long-range strikes on its oil infrastructure, saying such attacks continued despite repeated requests from US president Vladimir Putin for them to stop.

Kyiv says the attacks are a valid response to Russia's 2022 invasion, and designed to hinder Moscow's ability to fund its war.

Russia’s full-scale invasion against Ukraine may reach a “tipping point” next year that sees Moscow defeated, claims Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics.

While in New York to chair the United Nations Security Council, the politician argued that Russia is not genuinely interested in ending the war and likely viewed fresh negotiations on a ceasefire as a “decoy” to continue its aggression.

Meanwhile, Ukraine braces for a “perfect storm” of a brutal winter, increased attacks against energy infrastructure and escalating strikes against civilian targets.
